title: Dedicated capacity SKU matrix, contract response patterns, and surge graceband proposal
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: We need a merchantable SKU matrix and a standard set of contract/ security-questionnaire responses for Dedicated capacity customers that combines reserved GPU commitments, short-term surge lanes, and autoscale gracebands. This ticket proposes concrete SKU constructs, recommended pricing heuristics, and canonical answers for common enterprise security/contract questions to speed procurement and reduce legal back-and-forth.

Problem: Sales and Solutions Engineering report multi-week procurement slowdowns for Dedicated customers due to inconsistent SKU proposals and ad-hoc contract addenda for burst usage. Engineering also needs clear autoscale fallback rules to implement enforcement and telemetry. We want a repeatable pattern that balances revenue predictability (committed reserves), flexibility (surge lanes with pro-rated billing), and reliability (SLA tiers + gracebands).

Objectives:
- Ship a standardized SKU matrix (3 commitment tiers x 3 SLA bands + optional surge lanes) for sales playbooks and quoting calculators.
- Define canonical contract language for surge gracebands, preemption, and overage billing to include in Master Services Agreements and Security Questionnaires (SIG).
- Align runtime autoscale enforcement knobs and telemetry requirements with pricing (ENG deliverables: usage metering, pre-warn alerts, soft cap enforcement).

Scope: This is a product + legal + engineering alignment workstream. The ticket covers SKU definitions, example quotes, contract response text, security QnA templates, and a pilot plan for 2 enterprise customers. Implementation of enforcement in runtime is covered by ENG tickets in dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: SKU matrix published to pricing playbook doc and integrated into the quoting spreadsheet
Canonical contract language (MSA amendment + SOW snippet) drafted and approved by Legal
Security questionnaire (SIG-lite) template completed with agreed answers and storage classification guidance
Sales can produce a compliant quote for a dedicated + surge configuration within same business day
Pilot with 2 enterprise customers signed and telemetry shows correct metering for commits and surge within 2 weeks
proposal:
Recommended SKU constructs and billing rules:

1) Commitment Tiers (monthly):
- Core-16: 16 vGPU-equivalent reserved units; baseline p99 SLA (100ms target); price factor = base
- Core-64: 64 units; p99 stricter SLA (80ms); includes 10% free burst minutes; price factor = base * 3.2
- Core-256: 256 units; p99 premium SLA (50ms); includes 25% free burst minutes; price factor = base * 11

2) SLA Bands: standard / enhanced / premium with corresponding financial credit schedules (p99 breaches linked to credits capped at monthly commitment value).

3) Surge Lanes (optional add-on):
- Short-run surge blocks: 1-hour blocks purchasable in advance or auto-bid in near-real-time. Billed pro-rata based on reserve price * surge multiplier. Default surge multiplier = 2.5x for GPU-time.
- Graceband policy: soft cap allows up to 5% of monthly committed consumption as free soft bursts (absorbed into billing smoothing). Above soft cap, automated pre-warn at 80% of committed throughput and soft-throttle escalation.

4) Autoscale enforcement knobs (runtime alignment):
- Soft cap: allow spikes up to X% above commit (configurable per SKU) and queue or shed based on priority lanes.
- Default fallback: route excess to compatible lower-cost model variant or host region when capacity constrained.

5) Billing/Settlement: pro-rated invoices for partial-month changes; overage billed daily with itemized token-level usage records and line items for surge blocks.
pricing_heuristics: Base price per vGPU-hour derived from weighted blended cost (GPU amortized + infra + ops + margin)
Higher SLA bands priced at 1.5x and 2.8x relative to standard, adjusted by observed p99 delta and committed duration
Surge multiplier calibrated from backend marginal cost + premium for guaranteed immediate capacity; start at 2.5x and iterate from pilot data
Volume discounts applied on annual commitments using tiered curves (5% at 6 months, 12% at 12 months, custom beyond)
legal_and_qna_notes: Attach canonical answers for SIG-lite and common MSA addenda. Key clauses to include: capacity definitions, preemption & priority rules, surge billing example, SLA credit formula, data handling and audit access, KMS/HSM responsibilities, and upgrade windows. Sample QnA highlights: 1) 'How is dedicated capacity isolated?' => Describe tenant isolation model at control plane + node allocation. 2) 'Where are logs stored and for how long?' => Default 90 days with enterprise retention add-on. 3) 'Do you support customer-managed KMS?' => Yes (see Private deployment docs). Make all QnA answers vendor-neutral and provide reference links to internal runbooks.
sample_contract_snippets: Surge Graceband Amendment: Customer may exceed committed throughput up to a monthly graceband equal to 5% of committed GPU-hours. Exceeding graceband triggers auto-billing of surge blocks at published surge rates and triggers pre-warn notifications.

SLA Credit Language: For p99 latency breaches beyond SLA_Band thresholds, Redwood will issue a service credit calculated as (breach_seconds/total_seconds_in_month) * committed_monthly_fee, capped at 100% of monthly committed fee.

Autoscale Fallback Clause: If platform capacity constraints prevent immediate fulfillment of surge requests, Redwood will attempt fallback to a compatible variant or region. If fallback increases latency beyond agreed SLO, customer may request temporary rate-limiting or negotiated credits.
implementation_requirements: ENG: telemetry endpoints for committed vs actual GPU-hours and per-sku soft cap counters (ENG-23312)
ENG: billing pipeline changes to record pro-rated surge block usage and daily overage summaries
Legal: draft MSA amendment + SOW snippet for surge lanes
Sales/SE: update quoting spreadsheet and create 3 sample quotes for vectorized workloads, chat workloads, and embedding workloads
DX/Docs: dedicated capacity pricing page and SIG-lite template uploaded to Confluence
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly generous graceband causes under-recovery of marginal cost -> Mitigation: set pilot surge multiplier to 2.5x and review after 30 days
Risk: Legal pushback on fallback clause for regulated customers -> Mitigation: add explicit opt-out for Private deployments and offer isolated on-prem option
Risk: Telemetry gaps cause billing disputes -> Mitigation: require instrumentation and a 14-day roll-in period where metrics are validated before billing enforcement
Risk: SLA credit exposure unbounded -> Mitigation: cap credits to committed monthly fee and require customer acknowledgement in SOW
pilot_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): internal validation with billing sandbox and 2 reference customers (PS and SE-led). Phase 2 (30 days): signed pilot customers use SKU; collect telemetry and pricing outcome metrics; iterate on multipliers and soft-cap thresholds. Success metrics: less than 2 legal cycles to sign, average time-to-quote < 8 hours, pilot revenue at or above target ARPU, and billing disputes <= 1 per pilot customer.
notes: Feedback from Solutions Engineering on 2025-10-28 favored a pro-rated hourly surge pricing model instead of per-minute to reduce invoicing complexity. Customer interviews (two enterprise SaaS firms) indicated a strong preference for 1) firm pre-warn thresholds and 2) an explicit fallback guarantee or buyout option. Legal requested explicit retention and audit language for surge-related billing records.
